title: Gardenio — Edge Traffic Geomap (Phase-1 orientation console)
description: Orientation console for internet-facing edge traffic (design ka-0000007287#c3, epic ka-0000008216, task ka-0000003019). Reads the Traefik JSON access log in VictoriaLogs and orients a human by geography/ASN in ~10 seconds when the analyst loop escalates. The map is the CONSOLE, not the product (ka-0000007287#c2-3): it ships ZERO alerts — detection lives in the L2 rules + L3 analyst loop. Field names follow the edge log-field contract via the hidden f_* constant variables (sourceCountry / sourceASN / client_ip / DownstreamStatus / RequestHost / principal); if a per-env transport publishes different field names, adjust the f_* variables, never the panel queries. Depends on L0 transport (ka-0000001563) + L1 geo enrichment (ka-0000000583); inert/dark until both land and the datasource is wired.

list.name: f_country
list.label: Field: source country
list.description: Log field the enriched ISO-3166 alpha-2 country lands under. Default sourceCountry — the country dimension L1 (ka-0000000583) adds alongside sourceASN. Change only if the transport publishes a different field name.

list.name: f_asn
list.label: Field: source ASN
list.description: Log field the enriched ASN token lands under (auditxform.FieldSourceASN). Default sourceASN. Change only if the transport publishes a different field name.

list.name: f_sourceip
list.label: Field: client IP
list.description: Log field the client IP lands under. Default client_ip — the enriched scalar (the raw XFF chain stores as an opaque JSON-string that ipv4_range cannot filter; ka-0000006176). Change only if the transport publishes a different field name.

list.name: f_status
list.label: Field: response status
list.description: Log field the HTTP response status lands under (Traefik JSON access log: DownstreamStatus). Change only if the transport publishes a different field name.

list.name: f_host
list.label: Field: request host
list.description: Log field the requested hostname lands under (Traefik JSON access log: RequestHost). Change only if the transport publishes a different field name.

list.name: f_principal
list.label: Field: principal
list.description: Log field the authenticated principal lands under. Both L0 edge shippers now stamp the surface-agnostic 'principal' contract field (auditxform.FieldPrincipal): the Traefik adapter lifts ClientUsername and the AVA OCSF adapter lifts the Verified Access user identity, both normalised to '-' when unauthenticated (ka-0000005007). The prior value 'ClientUsername' existed only on Traefik rows and was itself '-' on 53,777 of 53,778 rows, so the post-compromise panels had no principal to attribute a novel geo to; the earlier 'principal' value was absent on every row and blanked every panel (ka-0000008216). Change only if a per-env transport publishes a different field name.

list.name: host
list.label: Host
list.description: Scope the whole board to one public hostname (e.g. cli.gardenio.example.com). * = all hosts.

list.name: principal
list.label: Principal
list.description: Scope the whole board to one authenticated principal. * = all (including unauthenticated hits).

list.name: gardenio rollout
list.textFormat: 3+ gardenio-system components restarted at once - a release deploy or chart apply. Check this marker before hunting a code cause for a step change on this board.

list.name: component restart
list.textFormat: gardenio-system/{{component}} moved its process start time - deploy, OOM-kill or crash-loop. Off by default: ~22 single-component restarts/day fleet-wide would bury the rollout markers.

options.content:
### Edge traffic geomap — orientation console (NOT the detector)

> **⚠ Inert by default — VictoriaLogs datasource not wired / edge log store empty in this environment.** Every panel below reads the **Traefik edge access log** via the **VictoriaLogs** datasource (`victoriametrics-logs-datasource`), which is **off by default** (`grafana.victoriaLogsDatasource.enabled=false` + `vlsingle.enabled=false`). The rows are **collapsed on purpose** so the board reads as intentionally-dark rather than a wall of datasource errors — expand a row only once the datasource is wired and the store is populated.

**This map is the CONSOLE, not the product** (design `ka-0000007287`#c2-3). It exists so a human can **orient in ~10 seconds when the analyst loop escalates** — nobody watches a map at 03:00 Sunday, which is when a competent APT operates. It ships **zero alerts** (Phase-1 = charts only). Detection lives in the L2 rules and the L3 analyst loop, not here.

**To light this board up:** set `grafana.victoriaLogsDatasource.enabled=true` **and** `vlsingle.enabled=true`, then land the edge L0 transport (Traefik access logs → VictoriaLogs, `ka-0000001563`) so the store is populated and the L1 geo/ASN enrichment (`ka-0000000583`) so `sourceCountry` / `sourceASN` exist. Field names are referenced through the hidden `f_*` constant variables — if a per-env transport publishes different field names, adjust the `f_*` **variables**, never the panel queries.

**Offline by design:** the map draws no external basemap tiles (this is a mirrored-image, default-deny-egress estate). Country geography comes from Grafana's **bundled** gazetteer (`public/gazetteer/countries.json`) + country-outline GeoJSON — same-origin, zero off-cluster fetch. The `gazetteer` option is resolved by Grafana as a **URL path**, never a friendly name: a bare `countries` fetches `/countries`, 404s, and silently drops every marker (blank map). A blank plane behind the country markers is expected and correct.

panels.title: Where is our edge traffic coming from? (request geo distribution)
Requests in scope
panels.description: Total edge requests matching the current host / principal / time scope.

defaults.noValue: no edge access records matched $host / $principal in this range — either the scope is too narrow or the edge log stream stopped shipping. Clear the filters and widen the range: if the whole board is empty the shipper is dark, not the internet.

targets.expr: ${f_host}:${host} ${f_principal}:${principal} | stats count() as requests

panels.title: Distinct countries
panels.description: How many countries the edge saw traffic from in scope — a spread in the ambient scanner floor, not by itself a signal.

defaults.noValue: no edge access records in scope, so country cardinality is UNKNOWN (not 0 countries). Clear $host / $principal and widen the range before concluding the edge saw no traffic.

targets.expr: ${f_host}:${host} ${f_principal}:${principal} | stats count_uniq(${f_country}) as countries

panels.title: Distinct ASNs
panels.description: How many autonomous systems the edge saw traffic from in scope.

defaults.noValue: no edge access records in scope, so ASN cardinality is UNKNOWN (not 0 ASNs). Clear $host / $principal and widen the range first.

targets.expr: ${f_host}:${host} ${f_principal}:${principal} | stats count_uniq(${f_asn}) as asns

panels.title: Distinct client IPs
panels.description: How many distinct client IPs hit the edge in scope.

defaults.noValue: no edge access records in scope, so client-IP cardinality is UNKNOWN (not 0 IPs). Clear $host / $principal and widen the range first.

targets.expr: ${f_host}:${host} ${f_principal}:${principal} | stats count_uniq(${f_sourceip}) as ips

panels.title: Requests by country (orient here)
panels.description: Edge request volume by source country — the 10-second orientation view. Marker size + colour scale with request count; geography is the bundled `countries` gazetteer (zero egress). Rename to `country` is what the gazetteer lookup keys on. This is the console: a bright new country against a quiet floor is a prompt to LOOK, never a page.

defaults.noValue: no edge access records in scope to place on the map — an empty map means “nothing matched”, never “no traffic reached the edge”. Clear $host / $principal and widen the range; if “Requests in scope” above is also empty the edge log shipper has stopped.

targets.expr: ${f_host}:${host} ${f_principal}:${principal} | rename ${f_country} as country | stats by (country) count() as requests | sort by (requests desc) | limit 300

panels.title: Top countries by request volume
panels.description: The map as a sortable table (the accessibility / colour-blind view of the same data). Scoped by $host / $principal.

defaults.noValue: no edge access records matched $host / $principal in this range. This table and the map above share one query, so they go empty together — check “Requests in scope” to tell “scope too narrow” from “shipper dark”.

targets.expr: ${f_host}:${host} ${f_principal}:${principal} | rename ${f_country} as country | stats by (country) count() as requests, count_uniq(${f_sourceip}) as distinct_ips, count_uniq(${f_asn}) as distinct_asns, max(_time) as last_seen | sort by (requests desc) | limit 300

panels.title: ASN concentration (who owns the address space)
Top ASNs by request volume
panels.description: Edge request volume grouped by source ASN — an APT campaign often concentrates in one or a few autonomous systems (design C2.1 campaign-shift tier). Sort by requests; a new ASN climbing the list is worth a look, not a page. Scoped by $host / $principal.

defaults.noValue: no edge access records matched $host / $principal in this range, so ASN concentration is UNKNOWN. Clear the filters and widen the range before reading this as “no campaign”.

targets.expr: ${f_host}:${host} ${f_principal}:${principal} | rename ${f_asn} as asn | stats by (asn) count() as requests, count_uniq(${f_sourceip}) as distinct_ips, count_uniq(${f_country}) as countries, max(_time) as last_seen | sort by (requests desc) | limit 200

panels.title: Request rate by top ASN over time
panels.description: Per-ASN edge request rate — a step-change in an ASN's share is the campaign-shift signal (charted, never paged in Phase-1).

defaults.noValue: no edge access records in scope over time — there is no ambient floor to draw, which means nothing matched the scope, not that the floor is zero. Clear $host / $principal and widen the range.

targets.expr: ${f_host}:${host} ${f_principal}:${principal} | rename ${f_asn} as asn | stats by (asn) count() as requests

panels.title: Auth-failure geography (where are the failures coming from)
Auth failures by country
panels.description: Failed edge responses (4xx/5xx) by source country — probes, scans and credential-stuffing land here (the ambient floor, design C2.1). Sized/coloured by failure count. Never sample non-2xx: failures ARE the signal. Geography via the bundled `countries` gazetteer.

defaults.noValue: no failed (4xx/5xx) edge responses matched $host / $principal in this range. A genuinely quiet window is possible here — but confirm “Requests in scope” is non-empty first, otherwise the whole stream is missing rather than the failures.

targets.expr: ${f_host}:${host} ${f_principal}:${principal} -${f_status}:range(100, 399) | rename ${f_country} as country | stats by (country) count() as failures | sort by (failures desc) | limit 300

panels.title: Successful vs failed responses over time
panels.description: Edge response outcome over time (success = 1xx–3xx, failure = 4xx/5xx). The failure floor is weather; a coordinated spike against one host is campaign-shift. Charted only.

defaults.noValue: no edge access records in scope — neither the success nor the failure series has anything to draw. Empty is “nothing matched”, not “100% success”. Clear $host / $principal and widen the range.

targets.expr: ${f_host}:${host} ${f_principal}:${principal} ${f_status}:range(100, 399) | stats count() as successes
${f_host}:${host} ${f_principal}:${principal} -${f_status}:range(100, 399) | stats count() as failures

panels.title: Auth failures by country + ASN
panels.description: Where failures concentrate, by (country, ASN) — the accessibility view of the failure map. Scoped by $host / $principal.

defaults.noValue: no failed (4xx/5xx) edge responses matched $host / $principal in this range. Cross-check “Requests in scope”: non-empty there plus empty here really is a clean window; empty in both means the stream is missing.

targets.expr: ${f_host}:${host} ${f_principal}:${principal} -${f_status}:range(100, 399) | rename ${f_country} as country, ${f_asn} as asn | stats by (country, asn) count() as failures, count_uniq(${f_sourceip}) as distinct_ips, max(_time) as last_seen | sort by (failures desc) | limit 200

panels.title: Campaign timeline (is the floor changing character?)
Request & failure rate over time (the floor)
panels.description: Total edge request rate vs failure rate over time — the ambient floor and its shape. A *change in character* (a new plateau, a coordinated burst) is the campaign-shift tier (design C2.1). Weather, not a pager.

defaults.noValue: no edge access records in scope — the ambient floor cannot be drawn. The floor is never truly zero on a public edge, so an empty panel here is a shipping/scope problem, not quiet weather.

targets.expr: ${f_host}:${host} ${f_principal}:${principal} | stats count() as requests
${f_host}:${host} ${f_principal}:${principal} -${f_status}:range(100, 399) | stats count() as failures

panels.title: New-country arrival rate over time
panels.description: Distinct source countries per bucket — a jump in geographic spread is a campaign-shift cue. Charted only.

defaults.noValue: no edge access records in scope, so per-bucket country spread is UNKNOWN (not “no new countries”). Clear $host / $principal and widen the range.

targets.expr: ${f_host}:${host} ${f_principal}:${principal} | stats count_uniq(${f_country}) as countries

panels.title: New-ASN arrival rate over time
panels.description: Distinct source ASNs per bucket — a jump in ASN spread often precedes a distributed campaign. Charted only.

defaults.noValue: no edge access records in scope, so per-bucket ASN spread is UNKNOWN (not “no new ASNs”). Clear $host / $principal and widen the range.

targets.expr: ${f_host}:${host} ${f_principal}:${principal} | stats count_uniq(${f_asn}) as asns

panels.title: Novel geo for a known principal (post-compromise orientation)
Successful authenticated requests by principal × country × ASN
panels.description: The crown-jewel orientation table (design C3 L2 post-compromise tier): a SUCCESSFUL authenticated request from a country/ASN that is novel FOR THAT PRINCIPAL is the strongest single edge signal of credential compromise. This board only ORIENTS — it lists every (principal, country, ASN) a working credential was seen from so a human can spot the novel one; the actual novel-vs-baseline detection + page is the L2 rule + L3 analyst loop, not this panel. Filter $principal to one identity, sort by last_seen. Scoped by $host / $principal.

defaults.noValue: no SUCCESSFUL authenticated edge requests matched $host / $principal in this range. Empty is the good state for the post-compromise view only if “Requests in scope” is non-empty — otherwise the records are simply absent and this panel is blind.

targets.expr: ${f_host}:${host} ${f_principal}:${principal} ${f_status}:range(100, 399) ${f_principal}:* | rename ${f_principal} as principal, ${f_country} as country, ${f_asn} as asn | stats by (principal, country, asn) count() as successes, count_uniq(${f_sourceip}) as distinct_ips, min(_time) as first_seen, max(_time) as last_seen | sort by (last_seen desc) | limit 300

panels.title: Raw edge access records (scoped)
panels.description: The most recent edge access-log records in scope — the drill-down after the map orients you. Scoped by $host / $principal.

defaults.noValue: no edge access records matched $host / $principal in this range — the drill-down has nothing to show. Clear the filters and widen the range; a permanently empty raw view means the edge log stream stopped shipping.

targets.expr: ${f_host}:${host} ${f_principal}:${principal} | rename ${f_principal} as principal, ${f_sourceip} as source_ip, ${f_country} as country, ${f_asn} as asn, ${f_host} as host, ${f_status} as status | stats by (host, principal, source_ip, country, asn, status) count() as hits, max(_time) as last_seen | sort by (last_seen desc) | limit 300

panels.title: Fan-out shape — is this one client or a spread?
Requests per client IP — p50 / p95 / p99 (fan-out shape)

defaults.noValue: no edge access records in scope — either nothing reached the edge under this scope, or the access-log transport is not publishing here

targets.expr: ${f_host}:${host} ${f_principal}:${principal} | rename ${f_sourceip} as source_ip | stats by (source_ip) count() as requests | stats quantile(0.5, requests) as p50
${f_host}:${host} ${f_principal}:${principal} | rename ${f_sourceip} as source_ip | stats by (source_ip) count() as requests | stats quantile(0.95, requests) as p95
${f_host}:${host} ${f_principal}:${principal} | rename ${f_sourceip} as source_ip | stats by (source_ip) count() as requests | stats quantile(0.99, requests) as p99

panels.description: Distribution of request volume across distinct client IPs in scope. A p99 far above p50 is a single loud client (scan or retry storm); p50 rising with p99 is broad traffic growth. This is the shape check that the count panels above cannot show.

panels.title: Auth-failure ratio in scope (now)

defaults.noValue: no edge access records in scope — either nothing reached the edge under this scope, or the access-log transport is not publishing here

targets.expr: ${f_host}:${host} ${f_principal}:${principal} | stats count() as requests, count() if (-${f_status}:range(100, 399)) as fail | math fail / requests as fail_ratio | fields fail_ratio

panels.description: Fraction of in-scope edge responses that are NOT 1xx-3xx. The floor is background internet scanning, measured at 6% over the default window and 11% over 24h on 2026-09-02 — so the thresholds sit at multiples of that floor (amber 25%, red 50%), not at zero. A jump into amber with request volume flat is a credential-stuffing or broken-client pattern; a jump with volume is a scan campaign, and the geo panels above say from where.

panels.title: Auth-failure ratio over time

defaults.noValue: no edge access records in scope — either nothing reached the edge under this scope, or the access-log transport is not publishing here

targets.expr: ${f_host}:${host} ${f_principal}:${principal} | stats count() as requests, count() if (-${f_status}:range(100, 399)) as fail | math fail / requests as fail_ratio | fields fail_ratio

panels.description: Fraction of in-scope edge responses that are NOT 1xx-3xx. The floor is background internet scanning, measured at 6% over the default window and 11% over 24h on 2026-09-02 — so the thresholds sit at multiples of that floor (amber 25%, red 50%), not at zero. A jump into amber with request volume flat is a credential-stuffing or broken-client pattern; a jump with volume is a scan campaign, and the geo panels above say from where. Ratio, unlike the count panels above, is immune to a traffic surge — it moves only when the *character* of the traffic changes.
